description: Dialogue for Severin Vane, a member of the Keepers who offers the Keepers initiation quest

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: You've been asking questions, and in the right order. Tharin trusts you, and Tharin does not hand that out. I'm Severin Vane, and I have work that doesn't go through the usual channels.

choices.text: I've dealt with the cultists at Willow Dale.
The phylactery. We need to talk about it.
The summoning at the ritual site is finished.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: The Keepers. We handle what kingdoms cannot admit is happening - cults, buried relics, doors that ought to stay shut. There are not many of us, and right now we have a problem.

choices.text: Why haven't I heard of the Keepers before?

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: I am a Keeper - part of an order that has existed for centuries. We protect the realm from threats that most people don't even know exist. Cults, dark magic, forbidden knowledge. We operate in secrecy because the truth would cause panic. But secrecy requires agents, and we need capable people like you.

choices.text: Tell me more about these threats.
I'm not interested in secret organizations.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: You shouldn't trust me - not yet. Trust is earned. But consider this: Tharin sent you to deliver a letter to me, didn't he? He trusts the Keepers because we've protected Elder Moor from threats he never knew existed. We're asking you to do the same. Prove yourself, and you'll see we're on the right side.

choices.text: Fair enough. What do you need?

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Because we're good at what we do. The Keepers have operated in shadows for centuries. Kings know of us. Some nobles suspect. But the common folk? They go about their lives never knowing how close they came to darkness. That's how we prefer it. Panic serves no one.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Call it what you will. When cultists summon entities that devour entire villages, we call it vigilance. When forbidden rituals threaten to tear reality apart, we call it necessary. You'll understand when you see it firsthand. Will you help us, or not?

choices.text: Tell me what needs to be done.
This is too much for me.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Not a conspiracy - a necessity. The world faces threats that most cannot comprehend. We stand between civilization and the void. You can believe me or not, but the darkness doesn't care about skepticism. It will come regardless. Will you help stop it?

choices.text: I don't believe in darkness from the void.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Willow Dale, northwest of Dalhurst. It was ours once, a watchpost, and we lost it decades ago to something that came through. We sealed it. The seals are failing, and there are cultists in the ruin now.

choices.text: What do you need me to do?
Why don't the Keepers handle this themselves?

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Go there. Break whatever rite they're working, and bring me back something I can read. I need to know how far down it goes.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Things from between. A cult opens the door, and what comes through is hungry, and what is nearby stops existing. Villages, mostly. That is the whole of it.

choices.text: What exactly do I need to do?

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: We have agents elsewhere dealing with other threats. The Keepers are few, and the darkness is many. We need local operatives who can act quickly. That's where you come in. Prove yourself at Willow Dale, and you'll be welcomed into the order. Are you willing?

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: 150 gold immediately. More importantly, you'll receive a Keeper's badge - proof of your affiliation. That badge opens doors, grants access to resources, and earns respect from those who know what it means. Plus, the Keepers take care of their own. Interested now?

choices.text: Deal. I'll go to Willow Dale.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Northwest of Dalhurst, in the hills. Kill the ones leading the ritual and bring me proof of what they were attempting. And be careful - what they're calling doesn't much care who is holding the knife.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: You're back. What did you find at Willow Dale?

choices.text: The cultists are dead. Their ritual is disrupted.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Show me the evidence. Ah... ritual components, summoning glyphs. This is worse than I thought. They were attempting to open a full breach. If you hadn't stopped them, half of Dalhurst would be a crater by now. You've proven yourself. Welcome to the Keepers.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Here's your payment - 150 gold and the Keeper's badge. Carry it with pride. You stand now among those who guard reality itself. There will be more work - darker threats, greater dangers. But also greater rewards. Welcome to the shadows, Keeper.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: I understand. This work isn't for everyone. If you change your mind, you know where to find me. Just remember - the darkness doesn't wait for us to be ready.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: You found it. I can tell by how carefully you are standing. So: where is it now? Think before you answer - I will believe whatever you say, and that is the problem with being asked by me.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Ash. Good. That is the answer the order exists to produce, and it is the answer nobody ever wants to give, because a destroyed thing teaches you nothing and a kept thing teaches you for years. Every Keeper who ever kept one had excellent reasons. We have a shelf of their names.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: You have it. On you. Now. ... Thank you for saying so - most do not, and the ones who do not are how the order learned to ask. Keep it, then. Keep it exactly as carefully as you are keeping it right now, and understand that the day you stop noticing you have it is the day it starts noticing you.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: They have it. ... No, do not explain. I have heard the explanations, and they are always sound, and they are always given by someone who was in a room with them and was not in a room with us. The order will move on this. You will not be told how. Take your payment - we pay for information, and you have given us a great deal.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Finished. Sit down and use small words, because I am going to have to repeat this to people who were not there. What came through?

choices.text: Nothing. I stopped it before the circle closed.
Something. Not all of it. It is still out there.
All of it. I was too late.
I stopped it. And I let Malachai live.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Nothing came through. Say that again in front of the order and watch grown men sit down. That is what we are for, and it happens perhaps twice in a Keeper's life. Paid, and thanked, and I would like you to hear the second one properly.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Partial. So there is a piece of something walking around with no idea what it is, and it will spend the next decade finding out. That is the outcome the order hates most - not a disaster, a project. You will be hearing from us about it. Paid.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: All of it. ... Then you were too late, and you came back anyway to tell me, which is more than the last three did. We do not punish that here. We write it down and we start again, and the writing down is the part that has kept this order alive for four hundred years. Paid. Go and sleep.

nodes.speaker: Severin Vane
nodes.text: Alive. Malachai is alive, and he knows the shape of the circle, and he knows your face. ... The order's position is that this was a mistake. My position, which is not the order's, is that a man who can be questioned is worth four who cannot, and I intend to question him for a very long time. Paid. Do not repeat any part of this conversation.
